title.en: Surface area and volume: cylinder, cone, sphere

text.en: A cone of ice-cream with a hemisphere on top: how much ice-cream fits, and how much wafer covers it? Surface area and volume formulae answer both.

Cylinder of radius r and height h: curved surface area = 2 pi r h, total surface area = 2 pi r (r + h), volume = pi r squared h.
Cone of radius r, height h and slant height l (l squared = r squared + h squared): curved area = pi r l, total = pi r (l + r), volume = 1/3 pi r squared h.
Sphere of radius r: surface area = 4 pi r squared and volume = 4/3 pi r cubed.
Hemisphere: curved surface area 2 pi r squared, total surface area 3 pi r squared, volume 2/3 pi r cubed.
For combined solids, add or subtract the parts that are visible or filled; surfaces that are joined together are not counted.
If a solid is melted and recast, its volume stays the same, so volume before = volume after.
Take pi = 22/7 unless the problem says otherwise.

problem.en: Find the volume of a cone of radius 7 cm and height 12 cm (pi = 22/7).

prompt.en: Write the formulae for the curved surface area and volume of a cylinder, cone and sphere.

requiredIdeas.en: 2 pi r h and pi r squared h
pi r l and 1/3 pi r squared h
4 pi r squared and 4/3 pi r cubed

commonMisconceptions.en: Using height instead of slant height for the cone surface

points.en: Cylinder: CSA 2 pi r h, V = pi r squared h.
Cone: CSA pi r l, V = 1/3 pi r squared h.
Sphere: SA 4 pi r squared, V = 4/3 pi r cubed.
Melting and recasting keeps the volume the same.
